back: A group of countries with no tariffs or quotas between members, each keeping its own tariffs on non-members.
A free trade area with a common external tariff on imports from non-members.
Preferential trade area, free trade area, customs union, common market, monetary union, full economic union.
Replacement of higher-cost home output by lower-cost imports from a partner in a trading bloc.
Switch of imports from a lower-cost outside supplier to a higher-cost member, because of the external tariff.

front: What does a **common market** add to a customs union?
back: Free movement of labour and capital between members.

front: Main cost of a monetary union to a member?
back: Loss of its own interest rate and exchange rate policy.

front: Why do commodity agreements often fail?
back: Cheating on quotas, new producers outside the agreement, and the cost of storing surpluses.
